notes:
K8Secret 0.6.10 — a kubeconfig that points at files which aren't there.

Your kubeconfig can supply a certificate authority, a client certificate, a key or a token either inline or as a path to a file. Paths belong to a machine. Copy a config from another Mac, or let a tool clean up the certificates it once wrote, and those paths resolve there and not here.

K8Secret used to treat a file it couldn't read exactly like a setting you never wrote — so it connected with no certificate authority and no client certificate, and the failure arrived several layers later as either a warning that the server was 'pretending to be' your cluster, or a bare TLS error. Neither mentioned a file, and both pointed at a cluster that was working perfectly.

It now stops at the kubeconfig and tells you which setting names a file it cannot read, what that path resolved to, whether it is missing or just unreadable, and which cluster or user it belongs to.

This is also the safer behaviour: K8Secret already refuses to fall back to your Mac's trust store when a cluster's certificate authority can't be parsed, so that it never trusts a certificate you didn't ask for. A missing file quietly went around that.
